jobs.occupation: Up to 3 PhD fellowships in Quantum error correction
jobs.description:
The Quantum error correction team at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) invites applicants for up to three PhD fellowships.

  The start date is (expected to be) 1 April, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The programme
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Program (NQCP), funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, is building a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge program in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, the ambition is to build a mission-driven full-stack approach which will involve exciting innovations at every level, from the quantum processor to the quantum-classical interface, all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. The vision of the programme is to enable the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve important problems in the life sciences.

  The project
 Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires low logical error rates together with resource-efficient, experimentally feasible approaches to quantum error correction. Our research spans low-overhead quantum error-correcting codes, efficient syndrome extraction, high-fidelity parity measurements, and scalable hardware architectures. We aim to connect these efforts with fault-tolerant logical operations, taking into account the noise characteristics, connectivity, and operational constraints of quantum computing platforms. In our work, we are collaborating closely with all of the different teams at NQCP; see nqcp.ku.dk.

  We are looking for up to three motivated PhD candidates to undertake research within theoretical effort for quantum error-correction. We are interested in developing a project plan with prospective candidates to best match their skills and experience to the activities in the QEC team. We imagine that the candidates would undertake research within one or more of the following topics:

   	
• Investigation of low-overhead and high-threshold error-correctable codes, including low-density parity check codes 	
• Resource estimation and optimization for scalable quantum computing over different hardware platforms 	
• Distributed quantum error correction on modular design and quantum networks 	
• Optimization of syndrome extraction circuits, error correction cycle, and fault-tolerant logical operation   Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of Physics, Computational Physics, Quantum Information, or a closely related field, with a focus on theoretical and/or computational quantum physics.

  Successful candidates will have:

   	
• Strong analytical and computational skills 	
• Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and quantum information 	
• An interest in developing quantum error correction methods that account for hardware capabilities and limitations 	
• A passion for developing theoretical protocols 	
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic research environment 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction or quantum computing platforms, including photonic systems and superconducting circuits, is an advantage.   Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by the NNF Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.

  The project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Maryam Khanahmadi, maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk, QEC team lead, and the principal supervisor will be Stefano Paesani, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed 
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. a degree in Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Quantum Information or similar. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full-time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Good language and communication skills 	
• Willingness to work in a team 	
• Willingness to engage actively with the other teams at NQCP    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Please note that there is the possibility of including an educational part to the PhD project. Therefore, please indicate in the application whether you would be interested in this.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original degree diplomas and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline
 The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You will be notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Maryam Khanahmadi: maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

You have a natural ability to communicate and collaborate across all levels of the organization, creating alignment, follow-through and ensuring that plans are translated into action. Most importantly, you are someone who takes ownership and gets things done.

jobs.occupation: Software Director - Industrial Automation, Robotics and Integrated AI
jobs.description:
Inwatec is looking for a Software Director to lead our software function and take product ownership of our Feeder platform. This is a broad leadership role for someone who can set direction, build strong software engineering capabilities, and stay close to customers, products, and execution.

Based at our office in Odense, you will lead approximately 15 software engineers across PLC, PC, AI, and Software Innovation. Three leads take responsibility for daily task coordination within these areas, while all employees in the software team report directly to the Software Director. You will also guide a cross-functional Feeder team as a new product moves into full-scale production and further maturity, while preparing for the next generation of solutions.

About Inwatec & the Laundrynerds

Inwatec develops industrial automation and robotics with integrated AI solutions for large industrial laundries worldwide and is recognized as an innovation leader in the industry. As part of the JENSEN-GROUP, we combine the speed and ownership of a focused growth company with the reach and opportunities of a global industry leader. We are building a scalable, high-performing operation while strengthening Inwatec as an innovation and software-engineering center of gravity for the wider group and industry. We love our informal work environment, where every idea is taken seriously, and everybody is treated equally. On Fridays, we meet at our bar for an after-work beer or some ping-pong. 

The Opportunity 

You will have two complementary mandates:

• Functional leadership: Own the capability, organization, and performance of the software function across PLC, PC, and AI.
• Product ownership: Lead priorities, customer value, and cross-functional execution for the Feeder platform.
You will report to Inwatec’s Managing Director and join the leadership team.

Key Responsibilities 

• Set and maintain the software strategy, architecture, engineering practices, tools, and development processes across PLC, PC, and AI.
• Contribute actively to Inwatec’s leadership team and optimize the company and JENSEN-GROUP as a whole.
• Lead approximately 15 software employees directly and develop the three leads for PLC, PC, AI, and Software Innovation, who coordinate tasks and provide day-to-day direction within their areas.
• Allocate software resources across product platforms in line with agreed half-year priorities.
• Strengthen platform compliance, technical quality, and cross-functional decision-making.
• Own the Feeder product roadmap, priorities, and customer outcomes within the agreed technical framework.
• Lead the cross-functional Feeder team through maturation and subsequent product development.
• Balance strategic direction with hands-on operational support, timely problem-solving, and coaching.

What We are Looking for 

• Leadership or substantial functional-lead experience in software engineering.
• Experience with software that enables physical products; industrial automation is strongly preferred.
• Strong understanding across PLC, PC, and AI domains, with particular depth in PLC or software close to machinery.
• Understanding of software platforms, architecture, tools, and engineering practices.
• Experience working across strategic, operational, and hands-on priorities.
• Product ownership experience or a strong customer and product orientation.
• A collaborative, enterprise-minded approach that puts company outcomes ahead of functional silos.
• A strong sense of ownership and pride in delivering on commitments.

How We Lead 

Our leadership culture is built on trust, constructive conflict, commitment, peer accountability, and collective results. We expect leaders to create a safe environment without lowering standards, give and welcome clear feedback, address issues directly, and help teams move from escalating problems to owning solutions.

Location and Working Model 

The role is based at Inwatec’s office in Odense, Denmark. Our standard working model is office-based. English is the corporate language; much of the everyday office conversation is in Danish, so Danish capability is preferred.

Why Join Inwatec? 

You will join a recognized innovation leader in the industrial-laundry industry, shape a growing software organization, and influence products used in demanding industrial environments worldwide. This is an opportunity to help scale an entrepreneurial company without losing its agility, customer focus, or collaborative spirit, with real responsibility across people, technology, product, and business outcomes.

How to Apply 

Please submit your CV and a short application as PDF explaining your experience with software-enabled physical products, leadership across multiple software domains and product ownership.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Dynamic Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Power-to-X Processes
jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a 24-month postdoctoral position in Dynamic Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Power-to-X Processes is available from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The project is primarily rooted in process engineering while also addressing interactions between Power-to-X plants and the electrical grid.

Your work tasks
You will develop and apply dynamic process models based on mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, reaction kinetics, and equipment behaviour to simulate integrated Power-to-X plants under changing operating conditions. The work will address renewable fuel production, particularly green methanol and sustainable aviation fuels through methanol-based and Fischer–Tropsch pathways. The work will focus on electrolysers, fuel-synthesis processes, energy storage, heat integration, and interactions with the electrical grid.

You will combine process simulation with operational optimization, process control, techno-economic assessment, and model validation to investigate flexible operation under varying renewable electricity generation and energy prices.

You will collaborate with academic and industrial partners, publish scientific results, contribute to project meetings and deliverables, and present findings at conferences and workshops. The position may also include limited teaching and supervision of bachelor’s and master’s students.

Your competencies
You hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, or a closely related field, completed by the application deadline. You have documented research experience in process modelling and simulation, preferably including dynamic modelling of chemical or energy processes.

Hands-on experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or Aspen Dynamics will be considered a strong advantage. Experience with gPROMS, Modelica, or comparable process-simulation tools is also relevant. Strong skills in MATLAB, Python, or a similar computational environment are expected.

Experience with Power-to-X, renewable fuels, optimization, process control, model validation, techno-economic assessment, or grid-integrated energy systems will strengthen your profile.

You will work closely with industrial and international partners. Therefore, the ability to translate research into practical solutions and communicate effectively across disciplines is essential. We value candidates who are proactive, structured, collaborative, and motivated to publish high-quality research and contribute actively to project activities.

Who we are
You will join the Fluid & Process research group at AAU Energy, Campus Esbjerg, where you will become part of an international and interdisciplinary research environment combining process, chemical, energy and electrical engineering. The group works with modelling, simulation, control, optimization and experimental validation of fluid and energy systems, with applications including Power-to-X, carbon capture and utilization, green fuels and sector coupling. The working culture is collaborative and informal, with close interaction among academic staff, postdoctoral researchers, PhD fellows and students. We share an ambition to contribute to the green transition through research with practical relevance. We offer laboratory and workshop facilities, and a collaborative environment that supports innovation, knowledge sharing, and professional development.

Learn more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Salary and terms of employment

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient retention in agricultural waters
jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies.

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling

• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data

• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures

• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals

Your profile

The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands

• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python

• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals

We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The successful candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management. The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department aims to be a supportive and encouraging workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer

The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information

For further information, please contact Senior Researcher Joachim Audet, joau@ecos.au.dk.

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than 1 December 2026.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

jobs.occupation: Technical Operations Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK
jobs.description:
Do you have solid technical know-how and a passion for contributing to the green transition? Then you might be our new Technical Operations Manager in Technical Asset Performance DK!

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Technical Operations Manager to join our dedicated Technical Asset Performance DK team. Based at our office in Hobro, you will be a central link between operations, projects and technical specialists.

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient retention in agricultural waters
jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies. 

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling
• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data
• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures
• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals
Your profile
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils
• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands
• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python
• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals
We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The successful candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management. The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department aims to be a supportive and encouraging workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer 
The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information
For further information, please contact Senior Researcher Joachim Audet, joau@ecos.au.dk.

Deadline

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant in Marine Taxonomy
jobs.description:
Do you have a sharp eye for marine species and want to put your taxonomic skills to work in both research and national monitoring? The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a 2-year position as research assistant in marine taxonomy, focusing on phytoplankton, macroalgae and benthic fauna. The place of work is Aarhus, and the position starts on 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2-year fixed-term position from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
Taxonomic expertise is the foundation of reliable knowledge about marine biodiversity, and of the monitoring that Danish authorities use to assess the state of the marine environment. You will help maintain and develop the department's taxonomic expertise and link it to new methods such as eDNA, ROV-based surveys and model-ling. Your tasks will include:

• Identification and quantification of phytoplankton, macroalgae and benthic fauna in samples from field surveys and monitoring programmes
• Data management, quality assurance and reporting as part of the department's advisory work for the Danish Environmental Protection Agency
• Contributing to research projects on marine biodiversity, e.g. in cultivated seaweed
You will work in close collaboration with experienced taxonomists and researchers at the Department of Ecoscience.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a Master's degree in biology, marine biology or a related field. We expect that you have:

• Documented experience in identifying marine organisms, preferably within phytoplankton, macroalgae and/or benthic fauna
• Experience with marine field work
• Experience with laboratory work and good laboratory practice
• Experience with data handling, quality assurance and reporting
• Good English skills, written and oral
• A structured and careful approach to your work and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team
It will be an advantage if you have:

• Experience with national monitoring programmes, e.g. NOVANA
• Experience with molecular methods such as eDNA, or with ROV or other image-based survey methods
• Skills in data analysis, e.g. in R
• An interest in research-based advice to authorities
Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience conducts national and international research and advisory projects covering all major subdisciplines within marine, freshwater and terrestrial ecology. The department is a recognised authority in research-based advice to Danish authorities and is responsible for large parts of the national monitoring of the marine environment. We are currently about 340 employees.

You will join the Section for Marine Ecology. Read more at AU Ecoscience - Research in marine ecology. For more information on the department, see https://ecos.au.dk/en/.

What we offer
The department offers:

• the opportunity to work with experienced taxonomists and to develop your skills within both classic and new methods
• a combination of field work, laboratory work, research and advice to authorities
• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark, and the area of employ-ment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information

For further information, please contact: Head of Section, Annette Bruhn, +45 2963 8034, anbe@ecos.au.dk.

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.
